DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF f*-IE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City 8 March 2021 http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 38 s.2021 HON. JIVY ROE C. BOMBEO Vice-Mayor Kidapawan City, Cotabato Dear Vice-Mayor Bombeo: This is in reference to your letter dated 14 December 2020 requesting this Department to declare Supplemental Budget No. 9 of Kidapawan City, Cotabato as null and void on the grounds of illegality and for being ultra vires. As culled from your letter, on 17 August 2020, Mayor Evangelista issued a notice of session scheduled on 18 August 2020 at 9:00 AM to deliberate and approve his request for the approval of the proposed Supplemental Budget No. 9 amounting to Twenty Million Four Hundred Twenty Three Thousand Nine Hundred Forty and 12/100 (Php 20,423,940.12) and authority to negotiate a loan of Php Two Hundred Forty Two Million (Php 242,000,000) with any reputable government bank to finance several projects of the city government. The said notice of session was received by your Office at 1:25 PM on 17 August 2020, without any attachment or any supporting document. On the same day, Mayor Evangelista wrote another letter, bearing the same content and tenor as the first one, but this time, the letter was marked with bold underline stating "Certified Urgent". Your Office and the Secretary to the Sanggunian received a copy of the said letter at around 2:55 PM on 17 August 2020 without any attachment or any supporting document, specifically that of the proposed appropriation ordinance authorizing Supplemental Budget No. 9 as well as the proposed resolution authorizing the negotiation of a loan amounting to Php 242 million.

On 17 August 2020, you issued a letter calling off the supposed special session dated 18 August 2020 for failure to comply with the rule that the notice of session must be submitted to the Presiding Officer at least one (1) day before intended session, as required by Section 52 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991 and Article 105 (2) (ii) of its Implementing Rules and Regulations. Moreover, the session was also called off for lack of material time for the Secretary to the Sanggunian to prepare the Order of Business and the lack of necessary documents to support the same as mandated by Section 1 of Rule VIII of the Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP). However, ten (10) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) wrote a notice of session dated 19 August 2020 calling for a special session on 24 August 2020 at 9:0AM to deliberate and approve the same matters previously requested by Mayor Evangelista in his letter dated 17 August 2020. The Sanggunian Panlungsod then proceeded to conduct a special session on 24 August 2020, wherein they unanimously agreed that the matter granting authority to the City Mayor to apply for a Php 242-million loan should be deferred. However, on the matter of ordinance approving Supplemental Budget No. 9, SP Member Ruby Padilla-Sison raised a point of order arguing, among others, that it was not proper for the Sanggunian to approve another supplemental budget as it would run contrary to Section 4 of Appropriation Ordinance No. 20-008, which declared that no subsequent supplemental budget or any appropriation will be approved without complying with the weekly reportorial requirements on the release, utilization and disbursement of funds in relation to COVID-19 and the donations received by the city government during the calamity caused by earthquakes. It is worthy to note that on 24 July 2020, you wrote a letter addressed to the City Accountant, Gina Ong, demanding the latter to render a report of funding, liquidation and utilization of the funds disbursed under Supplemental Budget Nos. 1 to 8, series of 2020. But Mayor Evangelista sent his reply and only attached a general report ion the fund utilization and status of program implementation for the COVID-19 related projects for the month of July 31 , 2020 and funded out of the BGCM and 20% Development Fund under Supplemental Budget No. 6.

Moreover, on 23 September 2020, you wrote a letter addressed to Mayor Evangelista requesting for the list of donors and the corresponding amount of donations, as well as its utilization and liquidation, in connection with the donations received by the City Government of Kidapawan in the aftermath of the earthquake that struck the city. Ostensibly, no report on the matter was rendered by the Office of the City Mayor. As such, you ruled that the request for the approval of Supplemental Budget No. 9 is out of order. Apparently, immediately after the special session was adjourned, eleven (11) SP members issued a notice of session calling for another special session on 26 August 2020 at 9:00am, purportedly to deliberate and approve the same subject matter- the ordinance approving Supplemental Budget No. 9, thereby disregarding your earlier ruling. However, said special session was called off in a Memorandum dated 25 August 2020 issued by you, for failure to comply with the requirements of calling a special session. Moreso, the subject matter of the supposed special session has been declared out of order. Said Memorandum was addressed to and received by the SP members as well as SP Secretary Cabelin and other members of the Sanggunian Secretariat. Despite being duly notified of the memorandum calling off the said special session, SP members conducted the "hurried" session and swift passage and approval of Supplemental Budget No. 9 on 26 August 2020. The SP members deleted the reportorial requirements which supposedly mandate Mayor Evangelista to submit a weekly report to the Sanggunian regarding the utilization of the funds. Hence, the subject letter-request. Based on your representation, Supplemental Budget No. 9 on 26 August 2020 was passed by the majority of the SP Members during the special session called for the purpose and thereafter, swiftly approved (we suppose, by the Mayor). Please be apprised that the Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare null and void any ordinance or resolution of the local sanggunian, or

any acts committed by the members thereof which is alleged to be a violation of the Local Government Code of 1991 or other applicable laws. Rather, RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 provides already a remedy or procedure to see to it that the ordinances or resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment program approved by a component city, like Kidapawan City, are within the powers conferred upon it, to wit: SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. - (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the Sanqqunian Panlunqsod or Sangguniang bayan shall forward to the Sanqqunianq Panlalawiqan for review. copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development pians and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) If the Sangqunianq Panlalawiqan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sanqqunianq Panlunqsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sanqqunianq Panlalawiqan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the correspondinq citv or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the Sanqqunianq Panlalawiqan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution the same shall be resumed consistent with law and therefore valid. (Emphasis Supplied) If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan failed to take action on Supplemental Budget No. 9 within 30 days after submission or after review, the said august

body finds Supplemental Budget No. 9 consistent with law and therefore valid, the next remedy is for you to file appropriate action before the proper forum. Jurisprudence is replete of cases holding that "(A) municipal ordinance is not subject to collateral attack. Public policy forbids collateral impeachment of legislative acts." 1 This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: NGAN, CESO Ill Icer-in-Charge Office of the Undersecretary for Local Government LLLS/27!17 Copy furnished: DIR. JOSEPHINE C.
